purpose: Visual design references; generated incidental content does not define product behavior.

images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished high-fidelity desktop interface design reference for TabPlayer, an actual Rust/Tauri guitar tablature editor. This image establishes the visual design for its session recovery dialog, a view absent from the user's supplied music-workstation collage.
Style: compact professional music workstation; flat charcoal navy panels #23272f on #171a20, fine #434b59 dividers, restrained #79aaff blue selected/focus states, system sans UI, clear 13px equivalent text, 3–4px corners. Warm cream notation paper is part of this product but do NOT show a playable editor behind this startup dialog.
Composition: one desktop screenshot 1280x800, centered 540px-wide modal in a subdued plain charcoal startup window. Small TabPlayer text in upper left window chrome. Dialog title "Recover unsaved work?" with hierarchy and useful breathing space. Under title exact copy "Restore documents from the last completed backup. Changes after that checkpoint may be missing." A small checkpoint timestamp row. Then "3 recoverable documents", a compact ordered list with three plausible original titles "Practice sketch", "Guitar arrangement", "Bass study". One subdued disclosure-like recovery details section with "One source file moved. Its recovered copy will open without a save path." At bottom right two real buttons "Discard recovery" secondary and "Restore" blue primary. No checkboxes, per-file checkmarks, extra settings, sidebars, meters, fake waveform, illustration, music logos, gradients, glass, invented actions, marketing text, or competing cards. Accessible contrast and a single blue focus ring around Restore. Output only the UI screenshot.

Use case: ui-mockup. Asset: high-fidelity desktop design reference for TabPlayer Export score dialog. Create a realistic screenshot matching a compact dark professional music notation workstation. Charcoal #171a20 backdrop, #23272f flat panels, fine #434b59 dividers, #edf0f5 text and readable #b5bfcc labels, restrained #79aaff blue focused/primary controls, 3px small corners, system sans. Screen1280x900. Center a modest 580px wide dialog titled "Export score" over a dim music workstation with warm cream notation paper, compact top transport and bottom overview barely visible. All typography crisp, orderly 28px controls, 12–16px grouping spacing, avoid nested card containers.
Dialog exact content top-to-bottom: "Export format" select with "Mixed WAV". "Tracks to export" section with three checked rows "Guitar", "Bass", "Drums". "Measures to export" section: unchecked "Measure range" checkbox, small text "All measures". Audio section a tidy two column form: "Sample rate" select "48 kHz"; "Bit depth" select "24 bit"; "Speed" select "100%"; "Effect tail (seconds)" input "2". Checked "Include backing", unchecked "Metronome". Small factual note "Audio export does not include count-in or progressive speed changes." Bottom divider then right-aligned "Cancel" neutral and "Export" blue primary buttons. No extra channels, spectral displays, animated meters, waveform, destination browser, compression options, per-track statistics, branding logos, product marketing or added controls. No glow, gradients, glass, decorative imagery. Output only screenshot.
